objects.description: Function pointer type for a test function used by fcyc. It points to a function that takes a pointer to long int parameters (an array or list of longs) and returns void. Intended to be invoked by the fcyc measurement routine to benchmark arbitrary test code using provided parameters. Calling convention and parameter semantics are up to the callee; only the signature is fixed.
Function pointer type to a function taking a single long int argument and returning void. Used to pass the element function whose performance (cycles per element) will be measured.

Enumeration selecting the sampling strategy when measuring performance. UNI_SAMPLE indicates uniformly spaced sample counts between bias*maxcnt and maxcnt; RAN_SAMPLE indicates randomly selected sample counts within the same range.

Enumeration selecting the error metric for least-squares fit evaluation: LS_AVG indicates average error, LS_MAX indicates maximum (absolute) error. Exact units and whether errors are absolute or signed are not specified in this header.

functions.name: fcyc
functions.signature: double fcyc(test_funct f, long int* params);
functions.description: Compute the number of CPU cycles used by a test function f when invoked with the provided parameters. Intended for benchmarking: f must match the test_funct signature (void (*)(long int*)) and interprets params as it chooses. Measurement behavior can be configured via the set_fcyc_* functions (e.g., cache clearing, K-best sampling, timer compensation).
requirements: f must be a valid, non-NULL function pointer of type void (*)(long int*).
params must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to memory that f expects to read/write; its layout/length must match f’s internal expectations.
f must not assume any specific cache state unless coordinated with set_fcyc_* settings; measurement may clear cache before runs if enabled.
Thread-safety and reentrancy of fcyc are unknown; callers should not assume it is thread-safe.

functions.name: set_fcyc_clear_cache
functions.description: Enable or disable clearing the cache before each measurement run performed by fcyc. Default is 0 (disabled).
requirements: clear is interpreted as a boolean-like flag (0 to disable, non-zero to enable); exact accepted range beyond this is not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements; ordering relative to fcyc calls matters.

functions.name: set_fcyc_cache_size
functions.description: Set the cache size used when clearing the cache during measurements. Default is 1<<19 (512 KB).
requirements: bytes is interpreted as a size in bytes; valid range and minimum/maximum are not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements that perform cache clearing.

functions.name: set_fcyc_cache_block
functions.description: Set the cache block size used during cache clearing for measurements. Default is 32 bytes.
requirements: bytes is interpreted as a size in bytes; valid range and alignment requirements are not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements that perform cache clearing.

functions.name: set_fcyc_compensate
functions.description: Enable or disable compensation for timer interrupt overhead during measurements. Default is 0 (disabled).
requirements: compensate is interpreted as a boolean-like flag (0 to disable, non-zero to enable); exact accepted range beyond this is not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements.

functions.name: set_fcyc_k
functions.description: Set K for “K-best” measurement selection used by fcyc. Default is 3. The framework attempts to select the K best samples within a tolerance.
requirements: k controls the number of best samples considered; required range is not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements.

functions.name: set_fcyc_maxsamples
functions.description: Set the maximum number of samples to attempt when searching for K-best within tolerance. If exceeded, the best sample so far is returned. Default is 20.
requirements: maxsamples is a count of samples; required range is not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements.

functions.name: set_fcyc_epsilon
functions.description: Set the tolerance (epsilon) required for K-best selection. Default is 0.01.
requirements: epsilon is a tolerance value; valid range is not specified.
Effect applies to subsequent fcyc measurements.

functions.name: find_cpe
functions.signature: double find_cpe(elem_fun_t f, long int maxcnt);
functions.description: Computes the cycles-per-element (CPE) for a function f whose work scales linearly with a count parameter, using default sampling/measurement parameters. Intended for quick CPE estimation for inputs up to maxcnt.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer of type elem_fun_t (i.e., a function taking a single long int argument and returning void).
f should perform work approximately linear in its count argument to make CPE meaningful (as implied by the header comments).
f must be well-defined and safe to call repeatedly for values of cnt in the range used internally up to maxcnt (exact set of cnt values is not specified).
maxcnt specifies the maximum count f supports for measurement; valid range is not specified in the header (caller should ensure values make sense for f).
f must terminate for all counts used during measurement; excessive side effects or non-determinism may skew results.

functions.name: find_cpe_full
functions.signature: double find_cpe_full(elem_fun_t f, long int maxcnt, long int samples, FILE *data_file, sample_t smethod, double bias, long int verbose);
functions.description: Computes the cycles-per-element (CPE) for function f with explicit control over sampling. Samples are taken between bias*maxcnt and maxcnt using either uniform spacing or random selection. If data_file is non-NULL, measurement data are printed for plotting (e.g., in Excel). Verbosity and other defaults can be adjusted via parameters.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer of type elem_fun_t (accepts long int, returns void).
f should perform work approximately linear in its count argument to make CPE meaningful.
f must be safe to call repeatedly for counts in the range [bias*maxcnt, maxcnt] as generated by the chosen sampling method; exact count set depends on implementation.
maxcnt denotes the maximum count allowed by f; the valid numeric range is not specified (ensure it is appropriate for f).
samples specifies the number of sample points; the header does not state valid ranges (use a positive integer for meaningful sampling).
data_file may be NULL to suppress data output; if non-NULL, it must be a valid, writable FILE* open to a destination suitable for textual data.
smethod must be a value of the sample_t enum: UNI_SAMPLE or RAN_SAMPLE.
bias scales the lower bound of the sampling interval (lower bound is bias*maxcnt); valid numeric range is not specified in the header.
verbose controls diagnostic output; semantics and accepted range are not specified in the header.
f must terminate for all generated count values; significant non-determinism may affect measurement stability.

functions.name: measure_function
functions.signature: double measure_function(elem_fun_t f, long int cnt);
functions.description: Measures and returns the number of cycles taken by function f when invoked with count cnt. It runs multiple trials until the best two measurements are within a 2% tolerance (TOL) of each other.
requirements: f must be a valid function pointer of type elem_fun_t (accepts long int, returns void).
f must correctly handle the provided cnt value; the valid range for cnt is not specified in the header.
f should terminate and be safe to call repeatedly; excessive variability may prevent convergence within the 2% tolerance.
The environment must permit stable timing/measurement; external interference may affect results (not specified but implied by timing measurement).

functions.name: start_counter
functions.description: Starts the CPU cycle counter measurement window. Typical usage is to call start_counter() immediately before the code section you want to time, then call get_counter() afterward to obtain the number of cycles elapsed since start. Details of the underlying timing source and thread-safety are unknown from this header.
requirements: Call this function before calling get_counter() to obtain a meaningful cycle count.
Caller should assume no return value; check results via a subsequent get_counter() call.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent use from multiple threads unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: get_counter
functions.description: Returns the number of CPU cycles elapsed since the most recent start_counter() call. If a timing anomaly is detected, the function returns 1e20 as a sentinel to indicate an error condition. Use this after start_counter() to measure elapsed cycles for a code region.
requirements: Should be called only after a successful call to start_counter(); otherwise the returned value may be meaningless or undefined.
Caller must check for the special return value 1e20, which indicates a detected timing anomaly, and handle it as an error case.
Return type is double; consumers should expect large values and potential precision limits for very long intervals.
Assumes availability of a cycle counter on the running platform; behavior on unsupported platforms is unknown.

functions.name: mhz
functions.description: Determines the processor’s clock rate using a default sleep time and returns it as a double. The function name implies the result is in megahertz (MHz). The verbose parameter likely controls diagnostic or progress output; exact semantics are not specified.
requirements: verbose is an integer flag; specific accepted values and their effects are not documented here.
The returned value represents CPU clock rate (units inferred to be MHz based on the function name).
May perform timing operations internally; required privileges or platform support for high-resolution timers are unknown.

functions.name: mhz_full
functions.description: Determines the processor’s clock rate with additional control over measurement accuracy via the sleeptime parameter, and returns it as a double. The result is likely in megahertz (MHz) based on the function name. Larger sleeptime values typically improve accuracy; the time unit for sleeptime is not specified in this header.
requirements: verbose is an integer flag; specific accepted values and their effects are not documented here.
sleeptime should be a positive, non-zero integer to obtain a meaningful measurement; larger values generally increase accuracy (exact units unknown).
The returned value represents CPU clock rate (units inferred to be MHz based on the function name).
May perform timing and sleeping internally; required platform timer/sleep support is assumed but unspecified.

functions.name: ls_slope
functions.description: Computes the slope (m) of the best-fit straight line y = m x + b for the provided data points using least squares linear regression. Typical usage: pass parallel arrays of x and y values and the number of points; the function returns the fitted slope as a double. Error handling/edge-case behavior (e.g., zero variance in x) is not documented; return value semantics in such cases are unknown.
requirements: xval must point to an array of at least cnt elements.
yval must point to an array of at least cnt elements.
cnt must be a positive integer and should be at least 2 to perform a linear fit.
The x values should not all be identical; otherwise the slope is undefined (division by zero in least squares).
All xval[i] and yval[i] should be finite doubles (no NaN/Inf); behavior otherwise is unspecified.
The arrays xval and yval represent paired observations at each index.

functions.name: ls_intercept
functions.description: Computes the intercept (b) of the best-fit straight line y = m x + b for the provided data points using least squares linear regression. Typical usage: pass parallel arrays of x and y values and the number of points; the function returns the fitted intercept as a double. Error handling/edge-case behavior (e.g., degenerate inputs) is not documented; return value semantics in such cases are unknown.
requirements: xval must point to an array of at least cnt elements.
yval must point to an array of at least cnt elements.
cnt must be a positive integer and should be at least 2 to perform a linear fit.
The x values should not all be identical; otherwise the corresponding slope is undefined and the intercept cannot be determined via standard least squares.
All xval[i] and yval[i] should be finite doubles (no NaN/Inf); behavior otherwise is unspecified.
The arrays xval and yval represent paired observations at each index.

functions.name: ls_error
functions.signature: double ls_error(double *xval, double *yval, int cnt, ls_err_t etype);
functions.description: Determines the fitting error of the least squares line y = m x + b for the provided data. According to the header, it returns either an absolute or average error. Based on the enum ls_err_t { LS_AVG, LS_MAX }, this likely means the average absolute residual (LS_AVG) or the maximum absolute residual (LS_MAX). The function probably recomputes the least-squares fit from the provided data. Exact error definition and behavior for invalid inputs are not documented.
requirements: xval must point to an array of at least cnt elements.
yval must point to an array of at least cnt elements.
cnt must be a positive integer and should be at least 1; if the implementation internally fits a line, at least 2 points and non-identical x values are needed to define the fit.
etype must be a valid ls_err_t value (LS_AVG or LS_MAX).
All xval[i] and yval[i] should be finite doubles (no NaN/Inf); behavior otherwise is unspecified.
The arrays xval and yval represent paired observations at each index.

data_types.description: A filesystem path string pointing to a location where a file can be created or truncated and written as text or binary. The function opens the path with fopen(path, "w") and writes textual measurement data to it. The path may include directories and a filename; it must be valid for creation on the host system and not require read access to existing content since the file is newly created.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() in the find_cpe_full fuzzer stub.
# The stub opens the returned path with fopen(path, "w"), so we should provide a path string that is
# syntactically valid on common platforms and likely writable.
#
# Strategy:
# - Generate short, portable, relative paths that typically resolve to a writable location
#   within the fuzzer working directory (e.g., "out.txt", "cpe_data_123.csv", "logs/run_1.dat").
# - Mix in simple subdirectories; many fuzz harnesses allow creating new files in CWD.
# - Avoid absolute paths and special device names. Keep under 256 bytes, overall buffer <= 4096.
# - Ensure path contains only safe characters.
# - Occasionally include extensions .txt/.csv/.dat to exercise text writing code paths.
# - Return as bytes; FUZZ framework will map this buffer to FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME string.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
EXTS = ["txt", "csv", "dat", "log"]
DIR_NAMES = [
    "out", "log", "logs", "tmp", "data", "measure", "results", "cpe", "bench"
]
BASE_NAMES = [
    "cpe", "data", "measure", "result", "out", "run", "sample", "stats", "trace"
]


def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a base name from list or random token
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = rng.choice(BASE_NAMES)
    else:
        base = _rand_token(rng)

    # Optionally add numeric suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        base += f"_{rng.randint(0, 9999)}"

    # Pick an extension
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    else:
        ext = _rand_token(rng, 2, 4)

    return f"{base}.{ext}"


def _rand_rel_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide directory depth 0..3
    depth = rng.choices([0, 1, 2, 3], weights=[50, 30, 15, 5])[0]

    parts: List[str] = []

    for _ in range(depth):
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            d = rng.choice(DIR_NAMES)
        else:
            d = _rand_token(rng)
        # optional numeric or token suffix for dir
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            d += f"_{rng.randint(0, 999)}"
        parts.append(d)

    parts.append(_rand_filename(rng))

    # Construct POSIX-style relative path to maximize portability for fopen
    path = "/".join(parts)

    # Occasionally prefix with a simple relative dir like "./" to ensure relative path
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path = "./" + path

    # Ensure total length reasonable
    return path[:240]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate a set of candidate paths; pick one based on seed randomness to vary outputs
    candidates = []

    # Favor shallow paths
    for _ in range(6):
        candidates.append(_rand_rel_path(rng))

    # Include a few canonical single-file names commonly writable in CWD
    canonical = [
        "out.txt", "data.csv", "results.log", "cpe.txt", "measure.dat"
    ]
    candidates.extend(canonical)

    # Possibly add a nested path with consistent dirs
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        d = rng.choice(DIR_NAMES)
        candidates.append(f"{d}/{_rand_filename(rng)}")

    # Choose one deterministically from the RNG state
    path = rng.choice(candidates)

    # Return as bytes with a terminating null half the time to exercise C handling,
    # but avoid embedding nulls as FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME likely expects a C-string without extra bytes.
    # We'll not append null to keep it simple and safe for fopen.
    data = path.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")

    # Ensure buffer size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data
